punchline: Three phrases keep grief heavy: it will last forever, it covers everything, it's my fault. Name them and you can question them.
thirty_sec: After her husband died, psychologist Adam Grant told Sheryl Sandberg about Martin Seligman's three Ps: permanence, pervasiveness and personalization. That's thinking the pain lasts forever, touches everything, and is your fault. She heard all three in her own head. Naming them didn't end the grief, but it gave her something to question.
question: When did you last catch yourself thinking always or never about a hard day?
